title: Reel three opening; Bunk Johnson at the Eagle Hall and the first clarinet
summary: Barnes says no one in his family played, and he first got a clarinet through Bunk after the Eagle Band at Eagle Hall.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: This is real three, Emil Bonds. We were talking about Buddy Petit, huh? That's right. Joe Petit. I mean Joe Petit, the vowel trombone. The vowel trombones. So they had the trombones in those little bands that went around house to house, huh? Oh yeah, but they didn't have the trombone that went around then, I remember. Oh, they didn't have trombone? No. No trombone. No trombone. I see. Well, when did you first start to pick up on an instrument, Mary? Your dad didn't play, did he?
No, my dad didn't play anything. But I was watching, and I thought I'd pick it up. Tell the children about it, Bunk is the first one ever quality for me. Bunk?
Well, that, uh, that was when I went down the gambling house.
But how old were you this time? Yeah.

Oh, I was about 17, 18 years old. And I was down there, in front of mine, Johnny Palo, to baseball position. And, uh, got in a crap game down there, which was the crap game out in winter. And I once, they went to the dog and my dad, and I was in the Monday night. And I was in the middle of the night. And then, we came on up here, making sure. I come on up here and, uh, stop at the Eagle Hall. Bunk was playing there, Eagle Band.
They had an Eagle Hall? Eagle Band. Oh, what did you say something about Eagle Hall? Is this the hall where the Eagle Band was playing? Was it a place called Eagle Hall?
Yeah. Yeah. It was playing there. Oh, real Eagle Hall.
Oh, really? So, uh, Dundee Taylor, it used to be on the farm.

Uh-huh. So, I stopped in there, and they got to recess with them, and they, I called them down to get a drink. They come along and got a drink, and a bunch of women's in there and men. All the drinks for the house. So, when I bought the drinks for the house, well, I bought the drinks with me. Paid for the walk out, and, uh, I could get drink, drink, and have people's milk. All the way down, it was. So, Buckland had a play. So, I went down there after crossing out. Went down there to him. He, uh, told him I wanted to climb. And, uh, we, uh, the way, the porch I was working up to about, once it was about eight or nine o'clock, I don't remember the time. It was eight or nine o'clock. I was just a nine o'clock. Is that right? And what were you playing before that? Wasn't playing nothing. We were on the flute.
